title: traffic-duplication-gateway: staged canary echo with tenant credit gating
creator: Anika Sharma
description:
Goal: implement a production-safe traffic-duplication gateway that can fan out live requests to candidate model variants for canary evaluation and A/B experiments while enforcing per-tenant cost budgets, strong isolation, and automated rollback triggers. The gateway must support credit-based gating, adaptive sampling based on runtime signals (latency, token-cost, error-rate), and minimal production latency overhead.

Scope: design and deliver the duplication controller and a rollout plan for staged canaries and continuous mirrors. Exclude long-term UI for tenants (Console integration tracked separately) but include telemetry hooks and billing tags for chargeback.

Design highlights and constraints:
- Duplication semantics: copy-and-send with read-only semantics to candidate endpoints. No state mutation through mirrors. Candidate responses are discarded by default; harvested for eval pipelines.
- Per-tenant credit buckets: each tenant has a configurable monthly credit for mirrored tokens. The gateway enforces an egress quota and stops mirroring once depleted unless tenant opts into emergency override. Credits are tracked by the controller and surfaced to billing/console via tags.
- Adaptive sampling: start with low fixed sample rate (0.1%) for new canaries then adapt up or down by a control loop that observes candidate latency delta, error spikes, and cost burn. The control loop uses exponential backoff when error-rate > threshold and increases sample rate when candidate stable and under budget.
- Isolation and PII: mirrored payloads are sanitized by default. Sensitive fields are surface-configurable; for regulated tenants the system must support a no-mirror policy. Mirrors inject minimal headers (X-Redwood-Mirror: true, X-Redwood-Mirror-Token) to ensure auditability.
- KV-cache and prefix reuse: to avoid cross-talk we will not share serving KV caches between production and candidate replicas. Candidate replicas will warm caches with independent prefixes to avoid noisy neighbor effects on prod latency.
- Backpressure and fail-safe: the gateway must be latency-aware; if duplication imposes tail latency > configured SLO margin, duplication is automatically gated downward. Also provide global and per-tenant kill-switches for rapid rollback.
- Cost accounting: every mirrored request is tagged so billing ingestion can attribute mirror token costs to tenant-specific mirror buckets. Provide a nightly reconciliation job to correct edge cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- Functional: gateway can mirror production traffic to a candidate model with per-tenant credits enforced and tags emitted for billing ingestion.
- Performance: additional p50 production latency increase must be < 2ms and p99 < 15ms for steady-state traffic on our test fleet.
- Safety: automatic mirroring shutdown triggers on candidate error-rate > 1% over a 5-minute window or token burn rate exceeding 1.2x forecast.
- Observability: metrics present in Console: mirror_rate by tenant, mirror_cost_burn, mirror_error_rate, mirror_latency_delta; traces show duplicated-branch correlation id.
- Rollout: canary pipeline can be enabled for 10 internal tenants in Phase 1 and scaled to 100 after stability verification.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Controller API and data model (2 weeks): tenant mirror config, credit bucket, sample policy, kill-switch.
2) Gateway duplication path (3 weeks): safe copy, header injection, token tagging, per-request credit check.
3) Adaptive sampler and budget manager (2 weeks): control loop and reconciliation.
4) Safety plumbing (1 week): kill-switches, egress quotas, auto-rollback hooks tied into rollout system.
5) QA and canary (2 weeks): integration tests, perf bench, internal tenant rollout.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 0: dry-run mode that performs duplication but discards outbound calls (no candidate invocation).
- Phase 1: small internal canary across staging tenants with low sample rate and strict budget.
- Phase 2: controlled external tenant pilots with billing tags and optional emergency opt-in.
- Phase 3: open to all customers with console controls.

Open trade-offs and notes:
- We considered reusing prod KV to reduce candidate latency and cost; rejected because it risks exposing prod cache state and adds tail-latency coupling.
- We will not attempt exact token-level billing in the first iteration; use per-request token estimates with nightly reconciliation instead.
- Security review required due to mirrored payloads and tenant billing linkage.

comments: 2026-02-20 - Triage: scoped initial requirement set. Decided to treat mirroring as opt-in per tenant and to enforce strict egress quotas by default. (Anika)

2026-02-25 - Architecture review with runtime and billing. Key action: add X-Redwood-Mirror headers and per-request billing tags. Runtime team asked to ensure KV cache isolation. (Diego, Priya, Mateo)

2026-02-28 - Prototype results: duplicate pipeline adds ~1.4ms median overhead in lab with synthetic traffic; p99 overhead spikes if candidate endpoint blocks on disk. Action: add timeout path and circuit-breaker. (bench notes: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/boards/mirror-proto)
2026-03-01 - Security sync: identified fields that must be redacted for regulated tenants. Security requested opt-out by tenant and an audit log for every mirror invocation. (Sarah - security)
2026-03-03 - Design decision: DO NOT share KV cache between prod and candidate to avoid tail-coupling. Candidates will warm caches independently using deterministic prefixes. (Diego)
2026-03-04 - PR opened for gateway skeleton: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1284. Need reviews from @runtime-eng and @billing. (ENG-REVIEW requested)

2026-03-05 - Next steps: implement credit bucket reconciliation job, add automated rollback hook into rollout service, and draft Console telemetry panels. Assigned QA to run mirrored traffic safety tests. (Anika)
Notes: dependency on ENG-33345 for tenant-aware routing and ENG-42021 for replica quotas. Coordinate schedules to avoid conflicts during canary.
